subject: Request: SLA amendment for batch inference latency — proposed stability buffer
messages:
From: Emily Ramos <emily.ramos@starlite.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA amendment request: batch inference latency and credits

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this — quick context from our ops team. Over the last three onboarding runs (Jul 18, Jul 24, Jul 29) we've seen sustained p95 latency spikes for batch payloads (1k+ concurrent inference tasks) during peak ingest windows. We've attached a CSV with sampled traces. These bursts are primarily affecting our nightly processing and are causing downstream job retries.

We like Redwood's performance overall, but the default SLA language (monthly uptime + single latency SLO) doesn't reflect this batched workload profile. Our procurement team has asked whether Redwood will accept a narrow amendment that:
- Adds a short-term "stability buffer" (a small daily allowance for batched-window latency before credits trigger) for the first 90 days post-cutover, and
- Adds a separate, measurable monthly latency remedy (a small additional credit if p95 > 500ms for more than X hours), with explicit carveouts for scheduled maintenance and customer-driven load patterns.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will consider a limited exception like this? If helpful, Starlite is open to a modest increase to committed capacity while the kernel optimizations are tuned. Attaching traces and an estimate of last month's bill.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Ramos
Head of Platform Operations, Starlite AI
Attachments: starlite_latency_snapshot_Jul2027.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Ramos <emily.ramos@starlite.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request: batch inference latency and credits

Emily — thanks for the detail and the traces. We're happy to review and propose a narrowly scoped amendment for onboarding. A couple quick items up front so we scope correctly:

1) Can you confirm whether these traces are from Hosted API or Dedicated (reserved) capacity?
2) Rough monthly spend so we can calibrate the credit amounts (I see the file but want the committed spend line item your procurement will reference).

I'll loop in Aditya and Laura for SLAs and Markus for runtime/ops tuning. My initial read: a time-limited stability buffer + a separate latency remedy bucket is reasonable as a pilot. We'll send a proposed amendment that preserves our standard uptime percentages but adds a measured, temporary exception for batched windows.

I'll follow up in 24–48 hours with a concrete proposal and a draft amendment (PDF) for your legal to review.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc:
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SLA amendment request — draft proposal for internal review

Forwarding Starlite's request. TL;DR: they want a 90-day onboarding exception for batched inference latency plus a separate monthly latency credit. I drafted a proposal below — please review and flag legal/ops concerns.

Proposed amendment (high level):
- Scope: Applies only to batch inference workloads identified by request header X-Redwood-Batch: true and limited to the first 90 days after go-live.
- Uptime: Keep standard uptime bands unchanged (no change to availability %).
- Stability buffer: Allow a daily grace window for batched windows: up to 30 minutes/day where elevated p95 is excluded from credit calculation. This is to let kernel tuning and warm-up settle.
- Latency remedy: If aggregated monthly p95 for batched workload > 500ms for more than 4 cumulative hours in the month (excluding maintenance and the daily stability buffer), Redwood will apply a latency credit equal to 5% of that month's invoice. This is additive to any availability credits that apply.
- Credit tiers (availability): to stay compatible with contracting, propose a conservative adaptation — not our full playbook, but a reasonable pilot: 
  * Monthly uptime >= 99.95%: no credit
  * 99.95% > uptime >= 99.9%: 8% of monthly invoice
  * 99.9% > uptime >= 99.5%: 20% of monthly invoice
  * uptime < 99.5%: 50% of monthly invoice
- Credit cap: Cap total credits (availability + latency) at 200% of the monthly invoice.
- Carveouts: Scheduled maintenance (72-hr advance notice window by opt-in), DDoS or third-party network failures, and customer-driven extreme load (documented spike > 3x committed QPS) are excluded.
- Metrics & measurement: Use Redwood's console telemetry (per-route p95 and uptime) as primary; allow Starlite read-only access for cross-checking.

Questions for the group:
- Aditya: does the stability buffer approach create any metric artifacts that would be gamed or misinterpreted in our telemetry?
- Markus: what is the ops cost to implement route-tagging for X-Redwood-Batch and to provide the extra per-route telemetry access?
- Laura: legal — how does this interact with our standard credit schedule and the carveouts you usually insist on? Any flags?

If we can get buy-in from ops/legal, I want to offer a 90-day pilot and measure results; if the pilot shows improvement we can sunset the buffer and keep the latency remedy as a feature in the SLA.

—Kim

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA amendment request — draft proposal for internal review

Thanks Kim — I like the narrow scope. A few suggested edits inline:

- Stability buffer: bump to 45 minutes/day for the first 30 days, then 30 minutes/day for the remainder of the 90 day pilot. Nightly batch processes often need the initial warm-up window.
- Latency remedy: change threshold to p95 > 600ms (we measured their traces; 500ms is within our normal variance) and keep the 4 cumulative hours threshold. Set latency credit to 4% of invoice (keeps financial exposure tighter while still giving remediation).
- Availability credit tiers: I suggest slightly lower percentages to protect runway for a pilot: 99.95-99.9 => 6%; 99.9-99.5 => 15%; <99.5 => 40%.
- Measurement: we should include a reconciliation process: Redwood provides telemetry and Starlite may raise a formal data disagreement within 14 days with a joint review window.

Markus: can you confirm complexity on route-tagging + read-only access? If it is low-friction we can include it as a term.

If Laura and Markus are OK, I think we present this to Starlite as a limited amendment: 90-day pilot, slightly revised metrics (p95 > 600ms), capped credits, and reconciliation path.

- Aditya

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Ramos <emily.ramos@starlite.ai>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 15:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed SLA amendment (90-day stability buffer pilot)

Emily — thanks for the traces and patience while we coordinated internally. Attached is Redwood's proposed amendment (PDF) reflecting the pilot approach we discussed. High-level summary of the offer: 

1) Pilot scope: 90-day stability buffer for batched inference workloads (identified by header X-Redwood-Batch: true).
2) Stability buffer timing: 45 minutes/day for days 1–30, then 30 minutes/day for days 31–90.
3) Latency remedy: If aggregated monthly p95 for batch workload > 600ms for > 4 cumulative hours (excluding stability buffer and scheduled maintenance), Redwood will apply a latency credit equal to 4% of that month's invoice.
4) Availability credit tiers (pilot): 99.95-99.9 => 6% invoice; 99.9-99.5 => 15%; <99.5 => 40%.
5) Credit cap: Combined latency + availability credits capped at 200% of monthly invoice.
6) Measurement & reconciliation: Redwood console telemetry is primary; Starlite may open a data dispute within 14 days; we'll run a joint review if disagreement is raised.
7) Carveouts: Scheduled maintenance (72-hr notice), major third-party network incidents, and documented customer-driven overload (>3x committed QPS) are excluded.

Attachments included: redwood_sla_amendment_draft_v2.pdf (attached), latency traces you provided (starlite_latency_snapshot_Jul2027.csv). If this looks acceptable, I've added a DocuSign link for a signature round (see HubSpot deal and DocuSign links below). Once signed we'll schedule a kickoff with Markus' team for route-tagging and telemetry access.

Next steps we propose:
- Starlite legal review the PDF and flag changes within 5 business days.
- If minor, sign via DocuSign and we'll start the 90-day pilot within 7 business days of signature.
- If major objections, schedule a 30-min sync next week to iterate.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/AMEND-STL-4821
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/123456789/STL-4821

Thanks again — looking forward to stabilizing the rollout.

Best,
